intelligence.essence:
- **HIS WORDS (19:22Z):** "You have the speedometers and you have the numbers on each of them. Not speedometers on some, numbers on others — you just have speedometers and numbers on each of them, you have it well balanced so it looks beautiful and readable."
- **THE RULING:** every board carries BOTH — the speedometer AND its numbers — on each of them, well balanced (neither dwarfs the other, aligned, legible), so it looks beautiful and readable.
- **NEVER A BOARD WITH A SPEEDOMETER BUT NO NUMBERS,** and never a board with numbers but no speedometer.
- **PASS-3 BRIEF AMENDED A FIFTH TIME** (§1c, §1 measurement, §1 must-not, §2, §9) and sent to the pass-3 coordinator the same pass.
- **CLOSES THE LAST LOOPHOLE IN SN-2558:** every board having a speedometer is not enough — every board must have the speedometer AND its numbers.
intelligence.human_view: A gauge without its number is decoration — pretty, but it tells you nothing. Numbers without a gauge are a ledger — true, but you have to work to feel them. A board needs both, together, balanced: the speedometer shows you, the numbers tell you, neither dwarfs the other, both aligned, both legible — so the board looks beautiful and reads at a glance. His ruling closes the last loophole in the coverage rule: it is not enough for every board to carry a speedometer — every board must carry the speedometer AND its numbers, on each of them. Balance is the standard the eye judges by: beautiful and readable, together.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a toy car with a speedometer but no numbers on it — you can see the needle move, but you don't know how fast you're going. And imagine numbers with no speedometer — you know the number, but you can't feel it. Dad says: "Every car gets both — the speedometer AND the numbers, together, balanced so neither one is too big or too small." Now every car is beautiful AND you can read it. That's the rule: both, on each, balanced.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, a little speedometer with no numbers is just a pretty picture, love — it tells you nothing. And numbers with no speedometer are just a list, dear — true, but you have to work to feel them. His ruling is that every board gets both, love — the speedometer and its numbers, together, well balanced, neither one too big or too small, so it looks beautiful and you can read it at a glance. Beautiful and readable, dear — together, always.
